column7: Symmetrical overdrive with high headroom; Level, Tone and Drive controls; made in Nashville with Switchcraft jacks, true bypass and 9V external power. First Edition matched-set documentation says circuits were hand soldered through-hole and designed/built/tested by Aaron Wahl.
column10: First Edition enclosure/finish and the three-knob Level-Tone-Drive layout are useful specimen clues. Do not treat the matched-set edition as a separate circuit generation without later evidence.

column7: Asymmetrical full-bodied overdrive/distortion with complex gain structure; three-knob control surface, true bypass, Switchcraft jacks, USA manufacture and 9V external power. First Edition matched-set documentation identifies Nashville production and through-hole hand soldering.
column10: The three-knob surface, asymmetrical gain character and First Edition Nashville build details are high-value identification markers.

column7: Op-amp based distortion developed with the Let's Play All YouTube channel; three controls (Gain, Tone, Volume), top-mounted jacks, 9V external power and Boneface artwork. FLB says it is distinct from the 1991 and was released in August 2023.
column10: Keep the 2025 Rated R Skeleton Key as a cosmetic limited edition using the same circuit, not a new generation.

column7: Four controls: EGO, DESTRUCTION, DRIVE and MOOD. Built in London with soft-touch relay true bypass; high-output design with interactive dual gain controls and a compact 126 x 88 mm enclosure.
column10: Control names, two interactive gain controls and the medicine-leaflet presentation are strong external identifiers. Preserve later documentation revisions separately from generation claims.

column7: Distortion with auto-filter and ring modulation, eight controls, separate bypass and tap-tempo footswitches, and relay true bypass; built in London. A 2021 V.1 demo establishes the product predates the 2023 GPX coverage, so 2023 is not used as the introduction date.
column10: This record is deliberately date-cautious: the 2023 census catches the pedal, but earlier evidence proves the product was already in existence. Version labels must not be inferred from the discovery year.

column5: 2023 catalog presence; introduction date needs reconciliation
column6: Enhanced RAT-style distortion with blendable analog octave-up, independent MOSFET boost, six clipping modes, LM308H-based distortion section and relay true bypass. Ukrainian circuit designer Volodymyr Zakernychnyi is identified in 2023 coverage.
column9: 2023 sources clearly document the product and feature set, but introduction timing is not fully resolved because community evidence places the pedal in 2022. Keep date uncertainty explicit.
